item.title: [26.05] vim: 9.2.0541 -> 9.2.1252
item.description:
I'm opening a backport to 26.05 of the Vim changes for the last four-ish months because of security advisories. See also: #541059, #543710.

LLM listing of the advisories.

Upstream security advisories (30)

Code or command execution from untrusted files:

Patch Issue Advisory
9.2.0561 python3complete code execution GHSA-52mc-rq6p-rc7c
9.2.0597 pythoncomplete code execution GHSA-65p9-mwwx-7468
9.2.0663 netrw code injection in local file deletion GHSA-vhh8-v6wx-hjjh
9.2.0678 zip.vim PowerShell code execution GHSA-x5fg-h5w9-9frf
9.2.0699 pythoncomplete code execution GHSA-ppj8-wqjf-6fp3
9.2.0735 Ex command execution in C omni-completion GHSA-mf92-v4xw-j45x
9.2.0839 code execution via keyword lookup GHSA-r5v6-q6j8-8qw2
9.2.0840 netrw code injection via bookmarks GHSA-rcr7-f3wr-22r2
9.2.0845 Ex command execution in C omni-completion GHSA-cx73-phcg-3j5g
9.2.0847 vimball code execution via .VimballRecord GHSA-r22p-fhw4-84p2
9.2.1011 Ex command execution in C omni-completion GHSA-r77m-8m55-rpr6
9.2.1090 Ex command injection in sign jump GHSA-x9jf-rjm6-vxqh
9.2.1177 rubycomplete code injection GHSA-4xgr-vqh2-xfx8
9.2.1178 rmd syntax pattern code injection GHSA-x2w5-pj55-7hpc
9.2.1201 cargo quickfix plugin code injection GHSA-x2w5-pj55-7hpc (as given upstream; same ID as 9.2.1178)

Memory safety:

Patch Issue Advisory
9.2.0565 terminal: out-of-bounds read in update_snapshot() –
9.2.0653 spell: out-of-bounds write in tree_count_words() GHSA-wgh4-64f7-q3jq
9.2.0662 spell: stack out-of-bounds write in dump_prefixes() GHSA-qm9w-fmpj-879h
9.2.0670 out-of-bounds read with text properties GHSA-f36c-2qcp-7gpw
9.2.0671 out-of-bounds read with sodium-encrypted files GHSA-c4j9-wr9j-4486
9.2.0679 out-of-bounds read with text property virtual text GHSA-ww8h-47xp-hp4w
9.2.0698 spell: out-of-bounds write in soundfold() GHSA-q8mh-6qm3-25g4
9.2.0725 spell: stack out-of-bounds write in spell_soundfold_sal() GHSA-m3hf-xcm3-xhm2
9.2.0841 heap overflow with > 65535 text properties GHSA-hm4g-pjfx-m27j
9.2.0842 stack buffer overflow in socket server GHSA-49m8-wwxj-mr69
9.2.0843 popup opacity mask out-of-bounds read/write GHSA-pmvp-6rcj-98p4
9.2.0844 use-after-free on JSON decode error GHSA-69ch-22ch-r887
9.2.0846 spell: heap buffer overflow in set_sofo() GHSA-9jqx-hgpr-6v64
9.2.1013 libvterm out-of-bounds access on CSI 8 t resize GHSA-vfc7-mhvm-gjp8
9.2.1014 undo file size check overflow (32-bit only) GHSA-cvc5-p4x9-3f9f

The python/ruby completion and sodium issues only affect vim-full, which has +python3, +ruby and +sodium.

Unlabeled fixes of the same kind

Sandbox bypass or command injection:

  • 9.2.0576: popup_create() not blocked in secure/sandbox mode
  • 9.2.0608: popup_setoptions()/ch_setoptions() missing secure/restricted checks
  • 9.2.0736: crafted file can execute commands via PHP omni-completion
  • 9.2.0869: insecurely set (e.g. modeline) 'indentexpr', 'formatexpr', 'includeexpr' or 'complete' evaluated outside the sandbox
  • runtime: missing fnameescape()/shellescape() in several runtime files (vim/vim@3fa4da4acb)
  • runtime: keywordprg escaping in the c, go, sshconfig, systemd and gitrevlist ftplugins; filename escaping in the cppcheck and gnat compiler plugins

Memory safety from untrusted input:

  • 9.2.0569: libvterm CSI 8 t out-of-bounds access from terminal output (first fix; completed by 9.2.1013)
  • 9.2.0623: crafted spell file: integer overflow leading to heap overflow
  • 9.2.0658: xxd -r: signed integer overflow on malformed input
  • 9.2.0697: overflow when parsing CSI keys
  • 9.2.0738: crafted swap file: out-of-bounds write during recovery
  • 9.2.0815: deeply nested regexp exhausts the C stack
  • 9.2.0963: crafted spell file: read past the end when sound-folding
  • 9.2.1113: use-after-free/double free in serverSendToVim()
  • 9.2.1147: buffer overflow with composing characters in the higher planes
  • 9.2.1151: heap underflow with diffopt inline:word on a zero-line block

Other use-after-free, overflow and double-free fixes reached through scripts, autocommands or allocation failure: 9.2.0603, 9.2.0618, 9.2.0642, 9.2.0724, 9.2.0808, 9.2.0932, 9.2.0987, 9.2.1017, 9.2.1026, 9.2.1065, 9.2.1082, 9.2.1129, 9.2.1187, 9.2.1214, 9.2.1219, 9.2.1222, 9.2.1223, 9.2.1248, 9.2.1250.

Only the version bumps are backported. The other vim changes on master (finalAttrs, upstream test suite in passthru.tests, explicit pixman, Lua 5.5 for vim-full, and their follow-ups) are left out.

item.title: {tor,mullvad}-browser: 15.0.26 -> 16.0
item.description:
blog: https://blog.torproject.org/new-release-tor-browser-160/ (if it's not here yet, it will be once https://gitlab.torproject.org/tpo/web/blog/-/merge_requests/642 is merged) tb changelog: https://gitlab.torproject.org/tpo/applications/tor-browser-build/-/raw/tbb-16.0-build1/projects/browser/Bundle-Data/Docs-TBB/ChangeLog.txt mb changelog: https://gitlab.torproject.org/tpo/applications/tor-browser-build/-/raw/mb-16.0-build1/projects/browser/Bundle-Data/Docs-MB/ChangeLog.txt firefox esr: https://www.firefox.com/en-US/firefox/153.6.0/releasenotes/ firefox security advisories: https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/security/advisories/mfsa2026-120/

it's that time! this release notably brings us up to firefox 153 esr, as well as adding support for aarch64-linux.

Closes #491286. we've been able to build for aarch64-linux, and even launch the browsers in binfmt_misc with qemu-user, but not do any sort of meaningful wide-scale testing since we don't have a graphical aarch64-linux machine. cc @mio-19 @DaVinci42 @affhp, as folks who have expressed interest in aarch64-linux support before and may be able to test.

backporting note: we will have to backport this change. the tor project will no longer be supporting the tb/mb 15.0 release series, nor does upstream mozilla support 140 esr (it's been eol since 2026-09-29, though the tor project backported security fixes on their own last release). programs which need security updates like browsers have always been an exception to the major changes restrictions.

i haven't gotten in any deep testing of tor browser yet, only mullvad browser (though i have been testing TB alphas periodically). will try to get back to TB in a few hours, but anyone else feel free to do so in the interim. its rather unfortunate that the major version updates are tied up with security updates :upside_down_face:
